findings: Mean WER about 1.0 (tiny.en) and 1.26 (base.en); ~0.65-0.75 even on the best sentences; only isolated words (Photosynthesis, oxygen, sugar, air, people, because, base, nearly every food) survive.

Sentence 5 (64 words) fails in a single ORT call (Expand node: invalid expand shape, input too long for the model); it only works when split per sentence and concatenated, so the app must chunk by sentence.
Sentence 2 (16 words) produced 17 s of audio and ASR loops: duration is far longer than expected, suggesting the duration predictor misbehaves on some inputs.
Numbers: twenty four/three hundred sixty five came out as digits "365" at best, "twenty four" not recognised. Not reliable.
Diagnostic at speed 1.0 gave the same unintelligible result (WER 0.67-1.06 on the sentences checked), so speed 0.8 is not the cause.
No clipping (0 samples at full scale, peaks 0.39-0.67) and no long silences (longest 0.44-0.74 s); the audio is non-silent speech-like but not intelligible.
limitations: ASR is a proxy for a human ear; tiny/base Whisper are weak on unusual voices and could under-rate somewhat-intelligible synthetic speech, but base.en agreeing with tiny.en and the severity of the errors (word salad, loops) point to a real quality problem.

Possible pipeline fault not excluded: phonemisation is via phonemizer (espeak WASM) with the spike token/style handling (style row chosen by text length), which may differ from the reference Kitten implementation. Phoneme strings looked plausible for sentences 1,3,4 (IPA with stress marks).
No espeak-ng/other-TTS control was available locally to prove the ASR path on clean speech; one listener-free check only.
Single voice, single run, 5 sentences; no human listening was done.
files: work/voice-check/s1..s5.wav (git-ignored scratch), sp10/ for speed 1.0 diagnostic

correction_2026_11_02.summary: The first check (mean WER about 1.0) exposed a bug in the spike, not in the model. Kitten's own Python reference on the same files is intelligible, and the browser pipeline is intelligible once fixed.
bugs: JavaScript \w is ASCII only, so the tokenizer split every IPA symbol and inserted a space token between sounds; fixed with a Unicode-aware pattern /[\p{L}\p{N}_]+|[^\p{L}\p{N}_\s]/gu
the npm phonemizer drops punctuation while the reference keeps it (preserve_punctuation=True); fixed by phonemizing the pieces between punctuation and re-inserting it
the reference synthesises one punctuated chunk at a time and picks the style row from the chunk length; whole-text inference of long input fails with an ORT Expand error

python_reference.tool: Kitten onnx_model.py logic, phonemizer + espeakng-loader, onnxruntime CPU

fixed_browser_pipeline.note: sentence 3 scores 0.35 only because Whisper writes numerals ("24", "365") for spelled-out numbers; the speech is correct
fixed_browser_pipeline.token_ids_identical_to_reference: 6 of 7 chunks; the 7th differs in one phoneme (four: o instead of open-o) because the browser espeak-ng build is older

correction_2026_11_02.remeasure: Real-time factors from the first spikes (including 0.26 on the Galaxy S8+) used the buggy tokenizer, which produced about 1.5 times as many tokens; re-measure with the corrected pipeline.
